title: The Courage to Be Disliked
author: Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga
short_description: Adlerian psychology as dialogue — separate tasks, discard the desire for recognition, and live in the present community.
content_text:
PART 1 — KEY LESSONS (OUTLINE)

1. You can change now

  • Adlerian view: not determined forever by past.

2. Separate tasks

  • Own your tasks; stop intervening in others’.

3. All problems are interpersonal

  • Courage in relationships is central.

4. Discard recognition

  • Freedom needs courage to be disliked.

5. Community feeling

  • Horizontal contribution over superiority.

PART 2 — THE COURAGE TO BE DISLIKED

A 30-Minute Read Summary

Chapter 1: Dialogue as method

Kishimi and Koga’s The Courage to Be Disliked teaches Adlerian psychology through a youth–philosopher dialogue. The form matters: questioning beliefs until new courage appears.

You are invited to argue with the book.

Change is presented as present choice, not endless excavation alone.

Trauma care still belongs with professionals when needed — use philosophy as orientation.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Engage the ideas in dialogue — change is framed as present choice.

Chapter 2: Deny trauma determinism carefully

Adlerians emphasize that we are not doomed by past events to one lifestyle forever; we choose meanings and goals now. This is empowering and risky if it dismisses real wounds.

Hold both: past shapes; present chooses response and goals.

Seek therapy for deep trauma while practicing agency.

Ask: what goal does my current lifestyle serve?

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Honor wounds and still choose present goals — avoid fatalism.

Chapter 3: Teleology over etiology alone

Adler looks at purpose of behavior — what future goal is this serving — not only past causes. Anger may pursue dominance; shyness may pursue safety.

Find the hidden goal of a sticky habit.

Choose a healthier goal.

Behavior change needs new purposes.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Ask what purpose a behavior serves — then choose a better goal.

Chapter 4: All problems interpersonal

Adler claims life tasks are interpersonal — love, work, friendship. Isolation problems still relate to how we face others.

Inventory relationship avoidances.

Practice one horizontal approach this week.

Loneliness often needs courage, not only comfort.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Face life tasks through interpersonal courage, not only isolation.

Chapter 5: Task separation

Separate tasks: what is my task vs another’s. Do not steal others’ tasks (controlling their feelings/choices) or abandon yours.

Parents and managers often fail here.

Ask: whose task is this feeling?

Offer help without takeover.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Separate your tasks from others’ — help without hijacking.

Chapter 6: Freedom and being disliked

If you need everyone’s approval, you are unfree. Courage to be disliked is courage to live your tasks honestly without harming others’ rights.

Not an excuse for cruelty.

Expect some dislike when you set boundaries.

Prefer respect over universal liking.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Accept that honest living risks dislike — without becoming cruel.

Chapter 7: Recognition hunger

Living for praise makes you a hostage. Discard the need to be recognized as a primary fuel.

Do contribution for its own horizontal joy.

Notice praise-chasing at work.

Quiet excellence can be enough.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Stop using recognition as primary fuel — contribute horizontally.

Chapter 8: Horizontal relationships

Vertical relationships rank superior/inferior. Horizontal ones treat equals contributing differently. Adler aims horizontal.

Catch superiority contests in conversation.

Praise without ranking souls.

Learn from others without self-contempt.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Build horizontal equal relationships, not superiority ladders.

Chapter 9: Community feeling

Gemeinschaftsgefühl — community feeling — is belonging through contribution. Happiness ties to usefulness in community.

Find where you contribute this month.

Community can be small: family, team, neighborhood.

Self-absorption shrinks meaning.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Grow belonging through contribution to community.

Chapter 10: Here and now

Life is decided in the present moment’s choices. Waiting for perfect past resolution forever stalls living.

Act on one present task today.

Use past as data, not jail.

Mindfulness of now supports Adlerian courage.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Decide and act in the present — don’t wait for a perfect past.

Chapter 11: Courage rehearse

Courage is practiced in small interpersonal risks: saying no, asking, apologizing, initiating.

Schedule one courageous micro-act daily.

Debrief kindly.

Stack courage like fitness.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Practice tiny interpersonal courage acts daily.

Chapter 12: Live the dialogue

Reread tense chapters when approval hunger spikes. Argue again. Choose task separation once today.

Teach horizontal relating to juniors.

Combine with Stoic control ideas carefully.

Begin with one boundary said calmly.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: When approval hunger spikes, return to task separation and one calm boundary.

Turn The Courage to Be Disliked into a ten-day curriculum. Underline actions onto the calendar; practice; raise difficulty slightly; teach someone; write a memo of what continues. Continuity beats binge motivation. Shrink to two minutes if you stall, then rebuild.

Weekly optional huddle: win, miss, ask. Measure approach days. Keep sleep and ethics intact. Revisit chapters when you drift. Identity averages returns. One variable change per cycle.

Let the book become weekday language with your crew. Progress that wrecks foundations is theater. Adjust kindly. Begin again without courtroom drama when you miss.
